correctness.rationale: Reconstructed 24 signed-permutation vertices (±1,±1,±(sqrt2-1)), 36 edges and 14 facets. The ordered-absolute-normal chamber 0<y<x<1 yields exact facet-crossing expression N=4+2[1<x+a y]+2[a<x+y AND y<1-a x]+2[y<x-a], a=sqrt2-1. Four threshold lines partition the chamber into six listed triangles/quadrilateral tiles, whose unit-normal spherical Jacobian is (1+x²+y²)^(-3/2), with 48 full-sphere chambers. Independent spherical solid-angle implementation gave four masses (0.151052693273...,0.500227288252...,0.281397356296...,0.067322662178...) summing 1 and expected count 6.52997997475809. For all 210,000 independent Gaussian directions, geometric original-edge counting matched the analytic piecewise formula exactly (zero other counts), and histograms matched within 0.00076. All-direction proof rests on exact inequalities and six-tile geometry, not finite random samples.
residual_risks: Solid-angle integration requires correct six-tile partition; explicitly verified analytic thresholds and high-density independent orientations but symbolic exact tiling proof follows source geometric identities.

The exact four-atom Haar central-section law, including separate octagon and positive decagon masses, solves the full natural face-count distribution rather than a mean or single tail. residual_risks: Natural finite solid, not a theorem about arbitrary truncated polyhedra.
